evidence-based = based on systematic research rather than opinion or tradition
scientific community = researchers as a group who share methods, journals and criticism
variable = a factor that can change in an experiment and may affect the result
finding = a result or conclusion that comes out of a study
groundbreaking = so new that it changes a field of study or practice
cutting-edge = using the newest ideas or technology in a field
state-of-the-art = the best and most modern available at the present time
innovation = a new idea, method or product that is put into use
pioneer = a person who is among the first to develop a new idea or method
obsolete = no longer used because something newer and better exists
trial and error = learning by trying different methods until one works
broadband = a fast, always-on internet connection to a home, school or office
encryption = turning data into a code so that only authorised people can read it
algorithm = a set of rules a computer follows to solve a problem or make a decision
cybersecurity = protecting computers, networks and data from attack or unauthorised access
digital footprint = the trail of data you leave through online activity
cloud computing = using remote servers on the internet to store data and run programs
database = an organised collection of information that a computer can search quickly
user interface = the screens, buttons and menus through which a person controls a program
bandwidth = the amount of data that can be sent over a connection in a given time
